title: Ind-finite finitely presented algebras over a contractible base are w-strictly local
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative w-contractible ring [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Let $D$ be a nonempty small directed poset and $(B_d)_{d\in D}$ a direct system of commutative $A$-algebras, with unital $A$-algebra transition maps. Assume each $B_d$ is finite as an $A$-module (generated by a finite list) and finitely presented as an $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B=\varinjlim_d B_d$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $B$ is w-strictly local: its closed points form a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, every point specializes to exactly one closed point, and every localization at a maximal ideal is strictly henselian [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Every closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ maps to a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The canonical maps induce homeomorphisms
$$(\operatorname{Spec}B)^c\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_d(\operatorname{Spec}B_d)^c,\qquad \pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_d\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}B_d),$$
where superscript $c$ denotes the closed-point subspace and $\pi_0$ has the quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. Zero algebras, empty spectra, and noninjective transition maps are allowed. No assertion that $B$ is w-contractible is made.

proof.text: For any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset B$, step 2 verifies the maximal-coordinate hypothesis in (3) of [lem-sfb-finite-contractible-diagram-localizations]. Hence $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is strictly henselian and $\mathfrak m\cap A$ is maximal. W-locality from step 2 and this strict henselianity are exactly w-strict locality [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. This also proves the assertion about closed points over $A$. The two inputs allow zero algebras and noninjective maps; when $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is empty the localization and closed-point assertions are vacuous.
